source.title: Pattern Selectivity is Not Task-Causal Structure: A Cross-Architecture Mechanistic Study of Composed-Task Circuits in 1B-Class Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether IOI circuit roles transfer to three other 1B-class models and finds different primary screens, with effects that vary by screen and metric. It presents this as evidence that specific circuits do not transfer uniformly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI baseline capability for the three models, but those baseline scores alone do not test a circuit version. It also cites the GPT-2 small IOI circuit as prior work; cited results are not recorded as rows. Its own IOI screen ablations, matched-random controls, and the reported name-mover/S-Inhibition union and late-layer ablations are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study applies the GPT-2 small IOI head-class decomposition (prev-token, induction, name-mover, S-Inhibition screens) to Pythia 1B, OLMo 1B and OLMoE 1B-7B. It uses group mean-ablation against matched-random nulls. It finds a different primary class in each model, and argues the specific circuit does not transfer (V3). It also shows that one IOI component's apparent role depends on top-1 versus logit difference (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude the screen-and-ablate recipe ports across models but the primary IOI circuit does not: Pythia is prev-token-primary with a redundant late-layer name-mover+S-Inhibition pathway, OLMo is S-Inhibition-primary, and OLMoE is name-mover-primary (as in GPT-2 small). They recommend reporting both top-1 and logit difference because of margin-only effects. They also assert GPT-2 124M does not solve IOI on their batch.
record.recipe_differences: Uses task-pattern selectivity screens, group mean-ablation, and matched-random controls across other models; it does not test the GPT-2 small 26-head circuit using its stated faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI ablation effects vary by model and candidate screen. In OLMoE, S-Inhibition changes logit difference (+3.95 to +0.95) while top-1 changes only +0.6 percentage points. Prompt distribution and ablation type are not varied.

fits_no_version.finding: On the study's own 500-prompt IOI batch, GPT-2 124M reaches only 13% top-1 and 57% IO>subject. The authors conclude it does not solve IOI. The prompt ends 'to ' (trailing space), which may differ from the original setup.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 small's IOI capability, and hence the setting for V1, depends on the prompt and tokenization format.

record.problems: Three models are tested at one final checkpoint each, and each model is a single pretrained checkpoint. The paper notes that primary-screen stability across pretraining seeds is untested. It does not test GPT-2 small’s circuit criteria, other prompt distributions, or alternate ablation types.
record.rows_left_out: No IOI screen-ablation results were omitted.

untested.parts: The GPT-2 small 26-head circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not tested. GPT-2 is used only for a baseline capability check.
No test of backup heads taking over after name-mover ablation. Pythia's 'redundant late-layer pathway' is an inference from union ablation, not measured compensation.
Other sizes and training checkpoints are not tested; each model is one final checkpoint. Component reuse across tasks is only noted qualitatively (multi-role heads in Table 4); it is not tested.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods or ablation types; one screen-and-mean-ablate recipe is used throughout.
Ablation type and IOI prompt distribution are not varied, and faithfulness/completeness scores are not computed. Only top-1 versus logit difference is compared.
No per-order (ABBA/BABA), per-template or more-names breakdown, and no alternate prompt formats.

missing.what: Single-seed matched-random nulls behind the Table 3 differentials: Pythia S-Inh about 6pp, OLMo S-Inh +5pp, OLMo NM -11pp, OLMoE NM -0.6pp, OLMoE S-Inh -1.6pp.

Head overlap across tasks: OLMo L12 H8 and OLMoE L12 H14 are both name-mover candidates and members of their induction circuits. Several Pythia IOI candidates (L13 H1, L12 H1, L8 H7) reappear in the VB screen.
Per-model logit-difference changes for the other IOI screen ablations are not reported; only the OLMoE S-Inhibition and Pythia union values are given.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 limits_scope label is replaced by supports: metric dependence is what V5 predicts. Control rows are linked to V3 only, and the states of within-1σ nulls are set to absent. The screens differ from Wang et al.'s path-patching classes: prev-token and induction are capability screens from synthetic batches, and the name-mover/S-Inhibition screens use attention patterns only. All results come from a single seed per screen and one checkpoint per model.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test GPT-2 small’s 26-head circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. GPT-2 small is discussed and cited as prior work.
It does not ablate the main name-mover heads and test whether backup heads take over.

Tests IOI screens in Pythia 1B, OLMo 1B, and OLMoE 1B-7B at one final checkpoint each. Does not test other sizes or training checkpoints, or whether components are reused for other tasks as a general claim.
Uses one screen-and-ablate recipe; it does not compare circuit-finding methods or ablation types.
Compares candidate screens and reports top-1 and, for OLMoE S-Inhibition, logit-difference effects. Does not vary IOI prompt distributions or ablation types.
Uses a 500-prompt, 50/50 ABBA/BABA IOI batch but does not report separate results by order, template, or number of names, or compare alternate prompt formats.

relationships.reason: Name-mover ablation drops top-1 by 18pp against a null of -0.5±5.1 (34×), matching the GPT-2 name-mover primary role (R11, R18).
relationships.display_finding: Name-mover ablation reduces top-1 accuracy by 18 percentage points against a null of −0.5±5.1, a reported 34× effect.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: R11 and R18 establish a selective causal contribution from screened name-mover heads; support is bounded to this class.

relationships.condition: Pythia 1B, name-mover screen alone and late-layer set
relationships.reason: Ablating the name-mover heads helps IOI (+7pp vs null +2.7±4.0), and the full L8–L13 set helps by 8pp. The authors class these heads as correlates (R3, R14, R21).
relationships.display_finding: In Pythia 1B, name-mover ablation improves top-1 accuracy by 7 percentage points against a +2.7±4.0-point null, while ablating layers 8–13 improves it by 8 percentage points.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Pythia 1B, name-mover screen alone and late-layer set
source_check.reason: R3 and R21 report improved IOI after these ablations; the authors classify the screened name movers as correlates.

relationships.condition: Pythia 1B, prev-token, S-Inhibition and union ablations
relationships.reason: GPT-2 classes are load-bearing only secondarily or jointly. The prev-token screen is primary (-82pp); S-Inhibition is secondary (-33pp vs -4.4 null); the union flips logit difference (R1, R4, R15, R20).
relationships.display_finding: In Pythia 1B, previous-token ablation reduces top-1 accuracy by 82 percentage points, S-inhibition ablation reduces it by 33 percentage points against a −4.4-point null, and combined ablation reverses logit difference.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Pythia 1B, prev-token, S-Inhibition and union ablations
source_check.reason: R1, R4 and R20 show recurring classes with different relative importance and a jointly load-bearing late pathway.

relationships.reason: Classical S-Inhibition is primary (-32pp, 4.8×), but name-movers are only weakly specific (-17pp vs -9.6±8.8, 1.8×) (R7, R8, R16, R17).
relationships.display_finding: In OLMo 1B, S-inhibition ablation reduces top-1 accuracy by 32 percentage points, a 4.8× effect, while name-mover ablation changes it by −17 percentage points against a −9.6±8.8-point null, a 1.8× effect.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R7–R8 and R16–R17 show S-Inhibition primary and name-mover specificity weaker, qualifying preservation of the class-role decomposition.

relationships.reason: S-Inhibition ablation leaves top-1 unchanged (+0.6 to +1pp vs null -10.6±13.5) but cuts logit difference from +3.95 to +0.95. The role is margin-only (R12, R13, R19).
relationships.display_finding: In OLMoE 1B-7B, S-inhibition ablation changes top-1 accuracy by +0.6 to +1 percentage points against a −10.6±13.5-point null but reduces logit difference from +3.95 to +0.95.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R12–R13 show a margin contribution without a top-1 loss, qualifying the behavioral role attributed to this screened class.

relationships.condition: Prev-token screen in OLMo and OLMoE; induction screen in all three models
relationships.reason: Prev-token ablation helps IOI (+6pp OLMo, +26pp OLMoE). Induction-screen ablation changes top-1 by only 1–3pp in every model. These screens were defined on synthetic batches, not IOI prompts (R2, R5, R6, R9, R10).
relationships.display_finding: Previous-token ablation improves top-1 accuracy by 6 percentage points in OLMo and 26 in OLMoE, while induction ablation changes accuracy by only 1–3 points across Pythia, OLMo and OLMoE; the screens were defined on synthetic batches rather than IOI prompts.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Prev-token screen in OLMo and OLMoE; induction screen in all three models
source_check.reason: R2, R5–R6 and R9–R10 show reversed or negligible ablation effects for these screened groups; this challenges transfer of the screens' expected causal roles.

relationships.condition: OLMoE 1B-7B, S-Inhibition screen, top-1 vs logit difference
relationships.reason: The same ablation shows no top-1 effect but a 3.0-point logit-difference drop, so the component's apparent role depends on the metric (R12, R13).
relationships.display_finding: The ablation caused no top-1 effect but reduced logit difference by 3.0 points.

tranche.reason: Cross-model causal ablations explicitly argue that shared attention-pattern classes need not preserve their causal importance or circuit implementation.

source_check.notes: Screened-group results do not establish a complete circuit decomposition or the absence of every possible IOI-specific head of a class. No matched-random logit-difference null is reported for R13; multi-study statements were checked only for claims about this study.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Name-mover ablation substantially reduces top-1, consistent with a name-mover primary role in this model (R11, R18).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Prev-token and S-Inhibition ablations reduce performance, while name-mover and late-layer ablations help it; the primary causal screen differs from the transferred name-mover account (R1, R3, R4, R21).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: S-Inhibition is the primary screen; prev-token ablation helps, and name-mover has a smaller, less-specific effect (R5, R7, R8, R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: S-Inhibition affects the IO-versus-subject margin but barely changes top-1, so its apparent role depends on the metric (R12, R13, R19).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI screen ablations across the three models
reader_labels.reason: Screen effects differ by model; in OLMoE, S-Inhibition changes logit margin substantially while top-1 is essentially unchanged (R1–R13).
